decisions.reason: As a low-cost complementary cleaning product tied to the firm's installed base of wood floors, it remains worth keeping open because it supports the core system offer and there is still little reason to abandon it.

The maintenance oil line fits the firm's core aftercare proposition and can continue to generate learning and cross-selling value at limited continuation cost, even if some model-level pruning could occur later.

This care line still merits being kept as an option for the oiled-floor segment, but its narrower niche and overlap with adjacent care products make later rationalization more plausible than for the broader care items.
The moisture-protection underlay strengthens the flooring system offer and likely costs little to continue, so management would keep it while demand and specification patterns become clearer.

The high-density underlay foam is still useful to maintain a complete system range, but because it is more commoditized and overlaps with other underlay solutions it remains the accessory most exposed to future pruning.
